issues.description: The exercise specifies an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide() (UML and problem text) and the template's Main.java references Rideable (e.g., Rideable[] rideables = new Rideable[]{...}). However, the solution repository defines and uses an interface named 'Mountable' (Mountable.java) and the classes Pig and Seal implement Mountable. At the same time, Rideable.java exists in the solution but is empty. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual entity (the interface for animals that can be ridden) will confuse students: they will implement or look for 'Rideable' as described in the problem/template, but the solution and its classes use 'Mountable', and the empty Rideable.java in the solution gives no guidance or signature to follow.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Recommended options:
1) Rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable, update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable, and populate Rideable.java in the solution with the method signature: String messageOnRide(); then remove the unused empty Rideable.java (or replace it with the populated one). OR
2) If 'Mountable' is the intended name, update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' everywhere (UML, description, and example code) and ensure the documentation and tests reference Mountable. Ensure there is exactly one interface name for the rideable concept and that its single method signature (String messageOnRide()) is present in the chosen interface file.
